drug_class: Weight loss medication (combination appetite suppressant and anticonvulsant)
purpose: This medication is used to help adults who are overweight or obese lose weight and keep it off. It is used along with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity. Your doctor may prescribe it if your weight is causing health problems like high blood pressure or diabetes.
how_it_works: Phentermine works by reducing your appetite so you feel less hungry and eat less food. Topiramate helps you feel full sooner and may also help reduce cravings. Together, these two medicines work as a team to make it easier for you to eat less and lose weight.
common_side_effects: Tingling or numbness in your hands or feet, dry mouth, constipation, trouble sleeping, dizziness, changes in how things taste, and feeling nervous or anxious. Some people also notice problems with memory or concentration.
warnings: Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — it can cause serious birth defects. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control and have a pregnancy test before starting. Do not take it if you have glaucoma or an overactive thyroid. Avoid alcohol. Tell your doctor if you have heart problems, depression, or kidney stones. It can raise your heart rate and may cause mood changes or suicidal thoughts. This is a controlled substance, so do not share it with others.
typical_dosing: You usually start with a low dose — one capsule in the morning (3.75 mg phentermine / 23 mg topiramate) for the first two weeks. Your doctor may gradually increase your dose over time up to the maximum strength. Always take it in the morning, never in the evening, because it can keep you awake at night.
